summary: Lane County, Oregon lookout: 1958 three-story tower replaced the cupola cabin; gone by 1985; first-structure date conflicts (1913 vs 1920-21); camera reactivated c.2012.

facts.agency: Western Lane Forest Protective Association and Oregon Department of Forestry
facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (1932); three-story Amort Special tower (1958)
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1985; the old cupola cabin was moved off the site in 1958

events.note: Register and firelookout.com date a platform tower and camp to 1913; the 1913 newspaper items only propose a lookout (conflicts with the 1920-21 house)
Trail and telephone line built to the summit
Weeks Law warden stationed on the summit through the summer; the collection dates this state forester's report entry 1914 (the report is cited as 1915)
H. M. Mayo, lookout; reported 160 forest fires in sight that summer (report dated September 13, 1917)
Lookout house put up by a carpenter after building materials were carried over a seven-mile trail; more material packed up on horseback in 1921
V. G. Backman, lookout; reported 76 fires from mid-June to July 31 (report dated August 9, 1924)
Newspaper notice that Verus Dahlin would be stationed on Prairie Mountain that summer
D-6 cupola cabin installed on the site
Polk-Benton District of the State Board of Forestry set to occupy and maintain the station under an agreement
Three-story Amort Special tower built as a joint Western Lane and Polk-Benton project; materials totaled $2,214.74, split evenly
Old cupola cabin moved half a mile east (register, firelookout.com) or about a quarter mile (collection); collection says it was bought by the Kyle Brothers and used as a line shack
Tower gone by 1985 (register); firelookout.com gives 1985; removal date itself not given
Long unused site reactivated with the Forest Watch camera detection system (c.2012)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date a platform tower and camp to 1913. The Oregon collection dates the first lookout house to 1920-21 and finds only 1913 plans. The story reports both and does not choose.
Half a mile east (register, firelookout.com) versus about a quarter mile (collection). The story reports both.
Aluminum-sided (register) versus wooden R-6 (firelookout.com). The collection describes it as an enclosed Amort Special without naming material. The story reports the disagreement.

sources.title: Oregon Department of Forestry's Wildfire Detection Camera System

notes_for_editor: Build date is unresolved; the story gives both the register's 1913 account and the collection's 1920-21 account. Last staffing record found is 1931 (a planned summer posting); a 1935 entry on the collection page is garbled and was not used. The warden entry is dated 1914 on the collection page (its report is cited as 1915), so the story uses 1914. Mayo's 160-fire report is dated September 13, 1917, and the story now places it in 1917. Backman's initials differ across 1924 items (F.G. in June, V.G. in August); the story uses V. G. as in the August report. The 2012 camera claim rests on one collection page (c.2012); no ODF or FPA listing names this site. The register lists 1958, 1982 and 2001 photos but gives no image URLs, so none were added. Access and what remains today: no source found. The undated 'Removed' label on the collection page was not used.
